t: You're on Great Ormond Street, in the London Borough of Camden. The street takes its name from James Butler, the 1st Duke of Ormonde. He was an Anglo-Irish statesman and soldier, and a lieutenant-general. He was known as Earl of Ormond from 1634 and Marquess of Ormond from 1642, and he became a duke in 1661. He inherited the earldom as a representative of the Kilcash branch of the Butler family, after the senior line failed. The spelling on the street sign differs slightly from his title, but the name is his.
